summary: The note summarizes the path to the impeachment of President Bill Clinton. Independent Counsel Ken Starr turned over documentation to the House Judiciary Committee, where Chief Prosecutor David Schippers and his team found sufficient evidence to impeach. Four charges were considered by the full House, two passed, and Clinton became the second president impeached, after Andrew Johnson in 1868.
one_line: Overview of how Independent Counsel Ken Starr's documentation led to the House impeachment of President Bill Clinton, with two of four charges passing.
key_facts: Independent Counsel Ken Starr turned over documentation to the House Judiciary Committee leading to the impeachment of Bill Clinton.
Chief Prosecutor David Schippers and his team reviewed the material and determined there was sufficient evidence to impeach the president.
Four charges against Bill Clinton were considered by the full House of Representatives.
Two of the four impeachment charges against Bill Clinton passed in the full House.
Bill Clinton became the second president to be impeached.
Andrew Johnson was the first president impeached, in 1868.
Clinton was only the third president against whom articles of impeachment had been brought before the full House for consideration.
Richard Nixon resigned from the presidency in 1974 while an impeachment process against him was underway.
Articles of impeachment were brought before the full House against Richard Nixon before his 1974 resignation.
